references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the paralyzed man who was carried to Jesus. Matthew describes the same event where a paralyzed man is brought to Jesus for healing.
Mark's parallel account of the paralytic carried by four men. Mark provides additional details that it was four men who carried him, and that they tore open the roof to lower him down.
Another healing of a paralyzed man (Aeneas) who had been bedridden for eight years. The parallel lies in the description of someone who is paralyzed (παραλελυμένος) and lying on a bed (κλίνη).
The paralyzed man at the Pool of Bethesda who had been sick for 38 years. A parallel situation where a paralyzed man cannot reach healing on his own and needs help from others.
Continuation of this account where Jesus heals the paralytic, and he picks up his bed and goes home – showing the result of men carrying the paralytic to Jesus.
Mark's account that the paralytic was healed, picked up his bed, and went out in front of everyone. Shows the outcome of the faith demonstrated by carrying the sick man to Jesus.
People carried the sick out into the streets on mats and beds so that Peter's shadow might fall on them. A similar situation where sick people are brought to the apostles for healing.
